newsitem.title: USA: Compaq, others unveil PC Theater initiative.
newsitem.headline: Compaq, others unveil PC Theater initiative.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp and Intel Corp unveiled an initiative to establish standards for a new category of computers for the home called the PC Theater.

Compaq and Intel said they are working with other leaders in consumer electronics and computing, including Thomson Consumer Electronics, Hitachi Ltd, Mitsubishi Electric Corp, NEC Technologies Inc and Toshiba Corp.
The focus of the initiative is to create a new category of home entertainment products that are compatible.

PC Theater is a new category of consumer entertainment devices that merge computing and traditional forms of media and entertainment content on large-screen displays. PC Theater products will feature TV viewing capability, surround sound audio, DVD (digital video disk) movies, wireless keyboards, mice and Web browsing.

The purpose of the initiative is to help ensure that consumers can have flexibility and choice. Compaq said these open standards it is proposing will allow large displays to connect with computers to deliver better picture quality and seamless integration with PC control devices.
The standards will be the first in a series of specification proposals meant to define standards for convergence in the living room. They will be brought before a standards committee for approval.
These standards will define elements such as picture quality adjustments, color purity, audio control, control integration between the system unit and display and enhancement of power management.
